questions.q: For what things is there a season?
questions.a: There is a season for every matter under the heavens.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say there is a time for in a person’s life?
questions.a: There is a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to pull up what was planted.

questions.q: What other times does the Teacher mention for people’s actions?
questions.a: There is a time to kill and a time to heal, and a time to tear down and a time to build.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say there is a time for regarding people’s emotions?
questions.a: There is a time to weep and a time to laugh, and a time to mourn and a time to dance.

questions.q: What else does the Teacher say there is a time for?
questions.a: There is a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, and a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say there is a time for regarding seeking and keeping?
questions.a: There is a time to seek and a time to lose, and a time to keep and a time to throw away.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say there is a time for regarding speaking?
questions.a: There is a time to be silent and a time to speak.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say regarding love and war?
questions.a: There is a time to love and a time to hate, and a time for war and a time for peace.

questions.q: What question does the Teacher ask about a worker’s hard work?
questions.a: He asks what profit a worker gains from his labor.

questions.q: What did the Teacher see?
questions.a: The Teacher saw the work that God gives to human beings to keep busy with.

questions.q: What did God place in people’s hearts?
questions.a: God placed eternity in their hearts.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say is the only good thing for people to do in life?
questions.a: The Teacher says the only good thing is to rejoice and to do good while they are alive.

questions.q: What is a gift from God?
questions.a: The ability to eat and drink and the good that comes from one’s work is a gift from God.

questions.q: Why can nothing be added to or taken away from whatever God does?
questions.a: Nothing can be added to it or taken away from it, because everything God does will last forever.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say about what happens now and what will happen in the future?
questions.a: The Teacher says that what happens now has already happened before, and what will happen has already happened too.

questions.q: What did the Teacher see in place of justice and equity?
questions.a: The Teacher saw wickedness in the place of justice and in the place of equity.

questions.q: According to the Teacher, whom will God judge?
questions.a: The Teacher said God will judge both the equitable and the wicked, because there is a time for every matter and every deed.

questions.q: What does the Teacher say God wants to show people about themselves?
questions.a: The Teacher says God wants to show people that they are like animals.

questions.q: How are people like animals?
questions.a: People and animals are from the dust, and both will return to the dust.

questions.q: What does the Teacher wonder about the spirits of people and animals?
questions.a: The Teacher wonders whether the spirit of a person goes upward and the spirit of an animal goes downward to the earth.

questions.q: What is the assignment for each person?
questions.a: The assignment for each person is to take pleasure in his work.

commentary.text: The changes of human affairs. (Eccl. 3:1-10) The Divine counsels unchangeable. (Eccl. 3:11-15) The vanity of worldly power. (Eccl. 3:16-22)

Eccl. 3:1-10 To expect unchanging happiness in a changing world, must end in disappointment. To bring ourselves to our state in life, is our duty and wisdom in this world. God's whole plan for the government of the world will be found altogether wise, just, and good. Then let us seize the favourable opportunity for every good purpose and work. The time to die is fast approaching. Thus labour and sorrow fill the world. This is given us, that we may always have something to do; none were sent into the world to be idle.

Eccl. 3:11-15 Every thing is as God made it; not as it appears to us. We have the world so much in our hearts, are so taken up with thoughts and cares of worldly things, that we have neither time nor spirit to see God's hand in them. The world has not only gained possession of the heart, but has formed thoughts against the beauty of God's works. We mistake if we think we were born for ourselves; no, it is our business to do good in this life, which is short and uncertain; we have but little time to be doing good, therefore we should redeem time. Satisfaction with Divine Providence, is having faith that all things work together for good to them that love him. God doeth all, that men should fear before him. The world, as it has been, is, and will be. There has no change befallen us, nor has any temptation by it taken us, but such as is common to men.

Eccl. 3:16-22 Without the fear of the Lord, man is but vanity; set that aside, and judges will not use their power well. And there is another Judge that stands before the door. With God there is a time for the redressing of grievances, though as yet we see it not. Solomon seems to express his wish that men might perceive, that by choosing this world as their portion, they brought themselves to a level with the beasts, without being free, as they are, from present vexations and a future account. Both return to the dust from whence they were taken. What little reason have we to be proud of our bodies, or bodily accomplishments! But as none can fully comprehend, so few consider properly, the difference between the rational soul of man, and the spirit or life of the beast. The spirit of man goes upward, to be judged, and is then fixed in an unchangeable state of happiness or misery. It is as certain that the spirit of the beast goes downward to the earth; it perishes at death. Surely their case is lamentable, the height of whose hopes and wishes is, that they may die like beasts. Let our inquiry be, how an eternity of existence may be to us an eternity of enjoyment? To answer this, is the grand design of revelation. Jesus is revealed as the Son of God, and the Hope of sinners.
